item.title: UAV-Based Federated Learning Incentive Mechanism for Latency-Aware Multimodal Target Tracking
item.description: Federated multimodal learning (FML) over uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks underpins privacy-preserving multimodal target tracking, yet energy-constrained and self-interested UAVs, which bear substantial sensing, training, and transmission costs, are reluctant to continuously contribute the high-quality multimodal data on which the global tracking model depends. To address this issue, this research aims to design an incentive mechanism that maximizes the aggregate FML efficiency and ensures economic fairness. This article proposes a novel two-stage incentive framework for UAV-assisted FML networks, modeled as a two-sided market between ground task requesters (TRs) and modality-specific UAVs. A TR purchases inference access to the updated multimodal target tracking model enabled by one UAV’s FML service. In the first stage, we develop a joint latency-modality-aware initial matching (JLMA-IM) algorithm. By constructing an FML-efficiency index that integrates physical-layer latency with modality importance, we cast the assignment as an aggregate-efficiency maximization problem and solve it exactly via a weighted bipartite matching approach. In the second stage, we design a double auction-based winner and pricing determination (DA-WPD) algorithm based on candidate critical pairs to determine final winners and transaction prices. We theoretically prove that the proposed mechanism satisfies individual rationality and budget balance, and that it is truthful under a boundary-stability condition. Simulation results show that the market-driven federated training achieves tracking accuracy comparable to full participation on 114 visible-thermal uncrewed aerial vehicle (VTUAV) sequences, JLMA-IM improves the FML efficiency by approximately 15% and reduces the bottleneck latency by up to 25%, and DA-WPD completes more transactions with higher social welfare than the McAfee double auction.

item.title: IFRM-CL: Risk-Modulated Dual-Loop Learning for Class-Incremental Fine-Grained Marine Debris Detection From UAV Imagery
item.description: Fine-grained class-incremental object detection (CIOD) for marine debris requires maintaining stable discrimination of previously learned categories while continuously incorporating novel categories. However, fine-grained marine debris classes often exhibit high visual similarity and subtle discriminative cues, which are prone to degradation during incremental updates, leading to cross-task interference and unstable decision boundaries. Existing methods mainly rely on replay, distillation, or pseudo-labeling strategies, yet fail to explicitly identify and protect fine-grained features that are most vulnerable to forgetting, leading to representation drift and weakened discriminative capability in critical regions. To address this issue, we propose an iterative forgetting risk-modulated continual learning (IFRM-CL) framework, which explicitly models and regulates fine-grained forgetting risk via a dual-loop optimization mechanism. Specifically, the inner loop performs fine-grained forgetting risk estimation by constructing a prior risk evaluation buffer (PRB) and computing a fine-grained forgetting risk index (FRI) to quantify task-level risk from both representation and decision perspectives. In the outer loop, a discriminative risk modulator (DRM) uses risk-guided gating to enhance fine-grained discriminative cues, with stronger modulation at higher estimated task-level risk and weaker modulation at lower risk. Through iterative interaction between the risk estimation in the inner loop and modulation in the outer loop, IFRM-CL forms a closed-loop update process that progressively refines feature adaptation based on risk and stabilizes the tradeoff between stability and plasticity. Experiments on MarineDebris-CL show improved overall detection performance and better retention of previously learned classes in the evaluated class-incremental setting.

item.title: Shadow-Aided Sparse Bayesian 2-D Autofocusing for High-Resolution Imaging of Moving Targets in Terahertz CSAR
item.description: Ground moving-target imaging (GMTIm) techniques present both opportunities and challenges in enhancing fine-grained situational awareness (SA) and target recognition. Compared with microwave synthetic aperture radar (SAR), terahertz-SAR (THz-SAR) offers higher Doppler sensitivity, enabling more effective detection of slow-moving targets (MTs). Moreover, its high carrier frequency and wide bandwidth facilitate high-resolution imaging. However, the substantial randomness in time-sensitive target motion can lead to severe range migration and azimuth defocusing, particularly at finer resolutions. To address these issues, we propose a shadow-aided 2-D sparse Bayesian autofocusing method for high-resolution imaging of MTs in THz circular SAR (CSAR). First, a CSAR echo model for MTs is derived, and 2-D velocity estimation is achieved by exploiting shadow information, which enables initial motion compensation. Second, considering that MTs typically exist only in specific regions of the scene and comprise a limited number of strong scatterers, indicating considerable sparsity, a 2-D autofocusing sparse Bayesian model is established by reconstructing the region-of-interest (ROI) echo after motion compensation. Finally, under a hierarchical Laplacian prior, refined GMTIm is realized by minimizing the image entropy (IE) of the range and azimuth signals, respectively. The proposed framework can adaptively handle unknown phase errors and significantly improve imaging quality. Simulations verify the accuracy of the 2-D velocity estimation and the resulting focusing improvement. Field experiments (with no accurate reference target velocities available) further demonstrate the imaging and autofocusing performance of the proposed method.

item.title: Real-Time Hardware Acceleration of Recursive Simplex Growing Algorithm for Finding Endmembers in Hyperspectral Imagery
item.description: Simplex volume (SV) is a widely used criterion which satisfies both abundance sum-to-one constraint (ASC) and abundance non-negativity constraint (ANC) for fully abundance constrained spectral unmixing (SU). It has been also used to develop endmember finding (EF) algorithms such as simplex growing algorithm (SGA). The main issue arising in SGA is its excessive computational complexity resulting from finding the determinant in SV calculation (SVC). To resolve this issue, orthogonal projection (OP)-based SGA (OPSGA) and geometric SGA (GSGA) are developed to remove the necessity of finding determinant. However, these two algorithms still require $O(L^{3})$ computational complexity with $L$ being the total number of bands. To further improve their computational complexity, an algorithm called recursive SGA (R-SGA) is developed to reduce the complexity from $O(L^{3})$ to $O(L^{2})$ in both data processing and storage memory. Moreover, a hardware architecture for R-SGA is physically implemented onto a field-programmable gate array (FPGA), which further divides the overall $O(L^{2})$ complexity into $O(L)$ resource complexity and $O(L)$ time complexity, making it the simplest, most efficient, and most performant hardware accelerated architecture to date for SGA. The hardware architecture is tested and validated by experiments performed on real hyperspectral image scenes, and fully characterized in terms of efficiency and performance for real-time applications.
item.authors: Minh Quan P. Tran;Lin Wang;Chein-I. Chang;

item.title: Viscoacoustic Least-Squares Reverse-Time Migration Using Wasserstein-2 Distance Objective Function
item.description: Least-squares reverse-time migration (LSRTM) has become an advanced technology for imaging complex subsurface structures because it can provide a migration image with higher resolution and more balanced amplitude than conventional reverse-time migration (RTM). However, the absorption and attenuation characteristics of the subsurface media will lead to amplitude attenuation and phase dispersion of the seismic wavefield, resulting in an inaccurate reflectivity profile obtained by LSRTM. In addition, since LSRTM is a linear inversion method based on the weak scattering assumption, its migration imaging results usually have high background model dependence. The traditional LSRTM is based on the $L_{2}$ norm as the objective function. When the background model is poor, the inverted result is easy to fall into a local minimum. To alleviate these issues, we propose a data-domain viscoacoustic LSRTM ( $Q$ LSRTM) algorithm based on the 1-D Wasserstein-2 ( $W_{2}$ ) distance objective function. In particular, we use the decoupled constant- $Q$ fractional Laplace viscoacoustic wave equation to describe the attenuation effect of the subsurface, and reduce the dependence of the LSRTM on the background model by using the $W_{2}$ distance objective function with better convexity. Since the $W_{2}$ distance in the optimal transport (OT) theory has better convexity than the $L_{2}$ norm, it can better avoid the inversion falling into a local minimum. In this article, we perform nonnegative normalization preprocessing on seismic data to meet the requirements of the OT distance for data. We verify the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed strategy by numerical tests of synthetic and field data. The migration results show that even in the case of a poor background model, $W_{2}$ -based $Q$ LSRTM can effectively compensate for the attenuation effect, improve the resolution, and suppress the migration artifacts in the inverted reflectivity profile.

item.title: PT2SF: Cross-Scene Similarity-Informed Point-to-Surface Learning for All-Day PM2.5 Field Reconstruction From Sparse In Situ Measurements
item.description: Hourly mapping of spatiotemporally continuous air pollutant concentrations remains challenging because ground monitoring networks are sparse, while satellite observations are frequently unavailable due to cloud contamination and the lack of nighttime retrievals. To address this limitation, we propose point-to-surface (PT2SF), a cross-scene, similarity-informed point-to-surface network for all-day air quality mapping from sparse in situ measurements. Rather than relying on geographic distance alone, PT2SF characterizes the environmental similarity between target pixels and monitoring stations using pollution, meteorological, and geographic attributes across multiple scenes. A graph attention network is developed to embed these similarity relationships to adaptively aggregate observations from environmentally analogous locations, including geographically distant stations, to infer continuous concentration fields. Evaluations using hourly PM2.5 measurements across China show that PT2SF achieves an overall correlation coefficient of 0.91 and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of $14.09~\mu $ g m−3, with stable performance across seasons and daytime and nighttime conditions. On a common testing subset, PT2SF yields an RMSE of $12.84~\mu $ g m−3, compared with $13.64~\mu $ g m−3 for Himawari-8 retrievals and $28.17~\mu $ g m−3 for Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) forecasts while maintaining hourly coverage independent of concurrent satellite retrievals. PT2SF also consistently outperforms classical interpolation and deep-learning baselines and shows substantially greater robustness to sparse observations. Under a 500-km station-masking radius, it retains a correlation coefficient of approximately 0.68, compared with 0.18 for inverse distance weighting (IDW). Feature analyses further indicate that relatively stable cross-scene similarity primarily determines graph connectivity, whereas dynamic meteorological conditions regulate short-term concentration variability. These results demonstrate that PT2SF provides an environment-aware and flexible framework for reconstructing continuous air quality fields from sparse observations and can be extended to other sparsely observed geophysical variables using variable-specific similarity descriptors.

item.title: Zero-OVCD: Bridging Training-Free Foundation Models and Pseudo-Label Learning for Open-Vocabulary Change Detection
item.description: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) enables the identification of user-specified land-cover changes in bitemporal remote sensing images, but existing training-free pipelines remain vulnerable to inaccurate candidate masks, ambiguous semantic assignments, and accumulated inference errors. To address these issues, we propose Zero-OVCD, a two-stage framework that uses no manual annotations. In the first stage, training-free, prompt-conditioned open-vocabulary inference generates high-quality change pseudo-labels through complementary candidate-mask refinement, multiscale semantic similarity fusion with margin-based reliability filtering, and response-guided mask correction and completion. These components jointly suppress noisy candidates, enhance mask-level semantic discrimination, and recover missed change regions. In the second stage, a category-specific change detector is trained using the generated pseudo-labels, while checkpoint voting and high-agreement sample selection are introduced to mitigate residual pseudo-label noise. On LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and S2Looking, Stage I achieves $F1$ -scores ( $F1$ ) of 86.25%, 85.82%, and 50.48%, while Stage II further improves them to 88.65%, 88.85%, and 57.96%, respectively. On SECOND, the macro-average $F1$ across six category-wise one-versus-rest tasks increases from 47.91% to 50.92%. These results demonstrate that bridging training-free foundation-model inference with noise-aware pseudo-label learning provides an effective solution for OVCD without manual annotations. The code will be available at https://github.com/1321663019/Zero-OVCD

item.title: Open-Set Domain Adaptation for Hyperspectral Image Classification via Adaptive Class-Aware Boundaries and Preserving Semantic Structure
item.description: In hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, domain adaptation techniques aim to address the scarcity of labeled data in the target scene. However, in practice, the target scene often contains land cover classes unseen in the source domain. This open-set setting introduces two core challenges: first, unknown classes in the target domain are prone to misclassification; second, forcibly aligning the entire target domain, including unknown classes, with the source domain not only leads to “negative transfer” due to interference from these unknown classes but also corrupts the intrinsic semantic structure of the target domain data. To tackle this challenge, this article proposes an open-set domain adaptation (OSDA) framework with a dynamic adaptive class-aware boundary (DACB) and target-domain semantic structure preservation (TSSP). The framework accurately identifies unknown class samples by dynamically learning an adaptive boundary for each known class and uses this boundary information to guide a weighted alignment, adapting only high-confidence known classes to mitigate negative transfer. Simultaneously, an entropy-driven self-supervised TSSP module minimizes the entropy of a joint neighborhood–prototype assignment distribution to strengthen high-similarity relations and suppress low-similarity relations. It further uses a prediction-entropy-based separation (ES) objective to repel potential unknown samples from known-class decision regions, thereby preserving the intrinsic semantic structure of the target domain and improving feature discriminability. Superior performance across multiple tasks and openness experiments on six different datasets demonstrates the proposed method’s effectiveness and robustness. The code is available at https://github.com/Li-ZK/ACBS-2026
item.authors: Mingtai Qi;Zhaokui Li;Yushi Chen;Wei Li;Xuewei Gong;Jing Tian;Jinjun Wang;Qian Du;

item.title: SAM-Guided Region-Aware Spectral–Spatial Learning Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification With Limited Samples
item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification with limited training samples remains challenging because sparse annotations provide insufficient supervision for learning reliable spectral–spatial representations. Existing label-efficient methods mainly exploit spectral and spatial information within the HSI, while region-level structural cues are often underused. To address this limitation, we propose SRSSNet, a segment anything model (SAM)-guided region-aware spectral–spatial learning framework for HSI classification with limited samples. SRSSNet first generates candidate region masks from HSI-derived visual representations using the SAM and refines them to construct a structurally coherent region prior map. The region prior map is then incorporated into a dual-branch network to guide spatial and spectral feature learning. In the spatial branch, a region-guided Transformer modulation (RGTM) module is proposed to aggregate region-aware tokens, perform contextual reasoning among regions, and use the enhanced tokens to modulate spatial features. In the spectral branch, a region-conditioned spectral calibration (RCSC) module is introduced to derive intraregion spectral statistics and calibrate pixelwise spectral embeddings through a gated residual mechanism. The features from the two branches are subsequently fused for classification. Experiments on three public HSI benchmarks under limited-sample settings demonstrate that SRSSNet achieves favorable performance compared with representative state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made available at https://github.com/YueLi-lab/SRSSNet

item.title: Vocabulary Lock-In in Remote-Sensing Open-Vocabulary Detectors for Cross-Taxonomy Disaster Damage Assessment
item.description: Rapid building-damage mapping from satellite and aerial imagery supports disaster response. Yet disaster-management agencies often use different taxonomies for comparable damage, so a closed-vocabulary detector must be retrained for each taxonomy. Open-vocabulary detectors (OVDs) accept textual class prompts and could adapt through prompt changes alone. Their performance on overhead remote-sensing imagery is insufficient without domain-specific fine-tuning, so practitioners fine-tune first and expect the prompt flexibility to carry over. This article identifies a previously uncharacterized failure mode in remote-sensing imagery processing: vocabulary lock-in, in which a fine-tuned detector loses access to a learned damage class when its training label is replaced by a semantically equivalent synonym. To explain this failure, we propose a diagnostic framework that asks in sequence how much lock-in occurs, when it develops during fine-tuning, and where it resides within the model. On a five-dataset disaster building-damage benchmark, a matched-granularity cross-taxonomy vocabulary substitution on FloodNet produces a mean 26.5% mean average precision (mAP)@50 drop, present in all five seeds. Of this drop, 16.3% is already present in the pretrained detector and 10.2% is attributable to fine-tuning. The same-domain direct-synonym substitution on the xBD test set, with images, annotations, taxonomy, and weights fixed, yields at least as large a relative drop. On Grounding DETR with improved denoising anchor boxes (DINO), training dynamics show that lock-in develops progressively during fine-tuning, while parameter-partition freezing localizes it to the grounding side. Strong weight-space constraints leave novel-vocabulary access unchanged, while direct decoder-attention measurements reveal prompt-dependent allocation under fixed weights. Our analysis therefore points to an activation-level access problem rather than weight drift. Based on this analysis, we introduce Embedding Bridge, a training-free method that expresses each unfamiliar class-name embedding as a weighted combination of familiar training-name embeddings. It restores access without changing model weights. It improves Grounding DINO on three of the four cross-taxonomy targets: by 6.8% mAP on FloodNet, 4.7% on RescueNet, and 1.7% on extensible building damage (EBD).
item.authors: Zhipeng Liu;Chunbo Luo;Wei Han;Christos Grecos;

item.title: TKA-WSCD: Integrating Text Prompts With Self-Distillation and Cross-Modal Feature Alignment for Weakly Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Remote sensing image change detection (CD) is essential for Earth observation and spatiotemporal analysis. However, fully supervised methods require extensive pixel-level annotations, limiting practicality and motivating weakly supervised approaches. A key challenge is that image-level labels provide limited prior information, making it difficult to accurately localize pixel-level changes. Vision–language foundation models offer a promising solution. Therefore, we propose TKA-weakly supervised CD (WSCD), a novel weakly supervised change detection framework that integrates text prompts with self-distillation and cross-modal feature alignment. TKA-WSCD extracts visual difference features from bi-temporal images via self-distillation and aligns them with textual descriptions based on a vision–language foundation model to improve accuracy. Specifically, we propose a DINOv3-based teacher–student bi-temporal self-distillation encoder, where the teacher network guides the student network via different fusion strategies to learn generalizable and robust visual representations of changed regions. Second, cross-modal alignment between textual descriptions and visual information is proposed to map textual and visual features of changed areas into a semantically consistent joint embedding space, generating alignment features that guide visual features to better discriminate changed areas. Finally, a text-guided cross-modal multitask objective function is designed, in which image-level classification, visual feature-consistency representations of the self-distillation network, and vision–text cross-modal alignment pixel-level segmentation are jointly optimized to achieve accurate change localization. Experimental results on WHU-CDC and LEVIR-CDC show TKA-WSCD obtains $F1$ -scores of 80.71% and 76.39%, outperforming mainstream weakly supervised methods and possessing prominent advantages in improving changed region integrity and accuracy under complex remote sensing scenes. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhangAilan/TKA-WSCD

item.title: SDENet: Synergizing Domain-Adaptive Structural Priors With Edge-Constrained Progressive Decoding for ORSI Salient Object Detection
item.description: Salient object detection in optical remote sensing imagery (ORSI-SOD) requires accurate region perception and reliable structural recovery. Despite recent advances, existing methods struggle with objects exhibiting strong directional variations, irregular shapes, and large-scale changes, resulting in blurred boundaries and incomplete regions. To address these challenges, we propose SDENet, a unified framework that synergizes domain-adaptive structural priors with edge-constrained progressive decoding for ORSI-SOD. Specifically, domain-adaptive structural priors are constructed through two complementary designs. First, we employ a SAM2 encoder with lightweight gated adapters to enable parameter-efficient transfer of pretrained knowledge to the remote sensing domain. On top of this, we introduce a structural context aggregation (SCA) unit that integrates directional perception with Mamba-based state-space modeling, allowing the model to capture directional cues, multiscale details, and long-range dependencies in a unified manner. The representations learned through these components further give rise to structure-adaptive priors, which provide more reliable guidance for salient object localization and shape recovery. To further improve boundary accuracy and region completeness, we design an edge-constrained progressive decoder that extracts multilevel edge cues and progressively injects them into each decoding stage. By jointly optimizing region reconstruction and boundary preservation, SDENet produces salient maps that achieve more accurate localization, sharper boundaries, and more complete object regions. Extensive experiments on public ORSI-SOD benchmarks (EORSSD, ORSSD, and ORSI-4199) demonstrate that SDENet consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative evaluation and visual quality. The code and results are available at https://github.com/zouduo/SDENet
item.authors: Yuzhao Wang;Duo Zou;Fuming Sun;

item.title: Physics-Constrained Dual-Prototype Learning Network for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) in hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) is challenging because the model can only access a few labeled samples from novel classes, while these novel classes may be spectrally similar to old classes despite belonging to different categories. When the base stage also contains few labeled samples, old-class prototypes may already be biased due to insufficient supervision. As similar novel classes are continuously introduced, such bias can accumulate and make old prototypes unreliable anchors, misleading novel prototype construction and blurring decision boundaries. However, existing methods mainly rely on feature similarity for prototype calibration or knowledge transfer, which may ignore physical relevance and introduce unreliable old-class information. Moreover, the old-class prototype structure may degrade during incremental learning, further aggravating old-class forgetting. To address these problems, this article proposes a physics-constrained dual-prototype learning network for few-shot class-incremental HSIC. First, a physics-constrained Mamba network is constructed to extract physically consistent features, and feature prototypes and physical prototypes are built for classification and physical relevance modeling. Second, a prototype structure distillation (PSD) module preserves old-class prototype relations to alleviate forgetting and local boundary degradation. Furthermore, a physics-guided prototype calibration (PGPC) mechanism is designed to calibrate novel prototypes according to physical relevance derived from physical prototypes, while maintaining sufficient margins between physically related old and novel classes. Experiments on three HSI datasets show that the proposed method outperforms representative FSCIL methods, demonstrating its effectiveness and stability.
item.authors: Chen Ding;Sirui Zheng;Pengfei Wan;Canyu Zhang;Yizhuo Dong;Wenqiang Hua;Song Yan;Lei Zhang;Wei Wei;

item.title: Multispace Distillation-Guided Teacher–Student Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to automatically identify surface changes by analyzing dual-temporal remote sensing imagery. While recent methods have introduced vision–language models (VLMs) to provide semantic guidance and suppress environment-induced pseudo-changes, they typically rely on direct feature fusion. This often compromises the high-resolution spatial details essential for RSCD or suffers from modality misalignment. A multispace distillation-guided teacher–student (MSD-TS) framework for RSCD is proposed to exploit frozen VLM knowledge through structured textual and visual prototype banks (VPBs), which serve as stable semantic anchors to guide the learning of a change-aware student network (CA-SN). The multispace distillation (MSD)-TS method consists of three key components: a semantic prototype-based teacher network (SPb-TN), the MSD strategy, and a CA-SN. First, the SPb-TN establishes a dual-branch backbone, where the frozen teacher network constructs a textual prototype bank (TPB) and a VPB that serve as structured semantic priors. Then, the MSD strategy bridges the two branches by enforcing the student’s features to align with these teacher-defined prototype banks via multilevel constraints, enabling efficient semantic knowledge transfer. Meanwhile, the CA-SN integrates a difference perception (DP) module and a channel–spatial attention (CSA) module to capture discriminative spatiotemporal changes. Finally, the learned features are fed into the detection module to generate the final detection map. Experimental results on three remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the MSD-TS method outperforms other existing RSCD algorithms.
item.authors: Wuxia Zhang;Xinyi Shi;Hailong Ning;Xueling Chen;Haifeng Zhang;Xiaoqiang Lu;

item.title: BSGA: Bitemporal Semantic Gated Adapter for Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Visual foundation models (VFMs) have substantially improved remote sensing change detection (CD). Existing VFM-based CD methods mainly improve task-specific adaptation and bitemporal interaction from different perspectives. However, the reliability of bitemporal difference discrimination under cross-temporal semantic inconsistency, caused by appearance variations, remains insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose the bitemporal semantic gated adapter (BSGA), a plug-in module that strengthens explicit bitemporal difference modeling and improves VFM-based CD. In particular, BSGA incorporates a prototype-guided semantic alignment (PGSA) module to enhance cross-temporal semantic consistency. The PGSA reconstructs semantic features for bitemporal remote sensing images with a shared set of learnable semantic prototypes. In addition, BSGA introduces a difference-semantic interaction gating (DSIG) module for feature modulation to highlight true changes while suppressing pseudochanges. The DSIG uses the feature difference between bitemporal images as a prior and combines it with reconstructed semantic contexts to guide the modulation process. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of BSGA for remote sensing CD. Moreover, BSGA can be seamlessly integrated into diverse VFMs, including DINOv3 and SAM2, to further improve CD performance.
item.authors: Fei Tong;Dou Quan;Ning Huyan;Pei He;Shuang Wang;Yunan Li;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: Collaborative Cross-Modal Fusion With Dynamic Enhancement and Reconstruction Guidance for UAV Object Detection
item.description: Cross-modal fusion detection utilizing visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) images has emerged as a promising solution for uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) perception, especially in complex or low-light environments. To alleviate the adverse effects of residual cross-modal feature misalignment, enhance multiscale representation, and reduce the computational overhead of fusion, this article proposes a novel collaboration cross-modal fusion (CCMFusion) framework that integrates three key components. Specifically, the dual-domain enhancement (DDE) module employs separate enhancement branches to improve feature discriminability along the channel and spatial dimensions, respectively, thereby highlighting object features while effectively suppressing background noise. The cross-modal interaction fusion (CIF) module integrates spatially aligned gated interaction (SAGI) and frequency-aligned guidance methods to align and exchange complementary information across different modalities, thereby capturing modality-specific cues and bridging semantic gaps. The cross-reconstruction and fusion (CRF) module further refines fused features via a reconstruction-based learning paradigm, combining a cross-modal guided reconstruction loss to preserve both shared and unique characteristics with a frequency-aware pooling strategy for global–local context integration. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle and FLIR datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an $mAP_{50}$ of 82.9% and an $mAP$ of 56.8% on the DroneVehicle, and an $mAP_{50}$ of 80.9% and an $mAP$ of 45.8% on the FLIR, significantly surpassing all compared approaches. The proposed framework provides a promising foundation for multimodal UAV perception and lays a solid foundation for future research, while practical edge deployment still requires further lightweight optimization. https://github.com/Caifei123/
item.authors: Fei Cai;Zhong Qu;Xuehui Yin;Yuhong Pan;

item.title: Multi-Information Collaborative Correction for Label-Quality-Robust Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Remote sensing image object detection has extensive application value in environmental monitoring, transportation planning, resource management, and military reconnaissance. Most current remote sensing image object detection methods heavily rely on accurate and high-quality labels for training. However, limited by the crowd-sourced labeling process, the nonintuitiveness of remote sensing objects, and the professional requirements for analysis in the remote sensing field, it is often challenging to obtain precise labels. To address this issue, we propose a multi-information collaborative correction-based label-quality-robust object detection (MICC-LROD) model. This model fully leverages category, detail, and spatial information to achieve a high-performance perception of objects in remote sensing images under conditions of low label quality. The model mainly consists of three core components: the category-detail information joint proposal (CDIP) miner, the spatial information-assisted proposal bag (SIPB) optimizer, and an alternating cascading arrangement. Specifically, the CDIP miner can fully capture the detailed features of objects in remote sensing images through its detail information perception branch. Meanwhile, it considers category and detail information during the proposal mining process, obtaining high-quality object proposals. The SIPB optimizer can comprehensively integrate spatial information within a wide receptive field to effectively optimize proposal bags, guaranteeing proposal mining and even the entire label refinement process. Furthermore, we arrange the miner and optimizer in an alternating cascading manner to achieve progressive correction, thereby enhancing adaptability to strongly noisy labels. A series of experimental results demonstrates that the MICC-LROD model can achieve high-performance object detection in remote sensing images with limited label quality of training samples and exhibits excellent adaptability when facing strongly noisy labels.
item.authors: Man Chen;Huaping Zhou;Kelei Sun;Antai Chen;

item.title: Seismic Blind Deconvolution Based on Nested EM–SMC Algorithm
item.description: Seismic blind deconvolution is an ill-posed problem due to the unknown source wavelet and reflectivity sequence. In this work, we propose a nested blind deconvolution method, which combines both the expectation–maximization (EM) and sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods for simultaneous estimation of both the wavelet and reflectivity sequence. In the proposed work, we initially assume priors for the wavelet, reflectivity sequence, and noise. The EM method estimates hyperparameters of the assumed priors. Meanwhile, SMC estimates the posterior distributions by leveraging the prior distributions within a Bayesian inference method. The proposed method is applied to synthetic, field, and well-log datasets for deconvolution. Quantitative metrics like signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), mean-square error (mse), and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) are used to evaluate the proposed method. The results indicate that the proposed method accurately estimates the wavelet and reflectivity sequence when applied to synthetic datasets, field datasets, and well-log datasets.
item.authors: Dokku Tejaswi;Nakka Shekhar;Anup Kumar Mandpura;Sunil Chinnadurai;Karthikeyan Elumalai;

item.title: Mapping of Greenland Ice Sheet Surface Melt Using Calibrated Multisystem GNSS-R Reflectivity
item.description: Monitoring surface melt over the Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) is critical for understanding ice sheet mass change and its climatic impacts. While microwave remote sensing has enabled long-term melt monitoring, its utility is often hindered by coarse spatial resolution, signal saturation during intense melt events, and diminished sensitivity to shallow melting. In this study, a calibrated multisystem reflectivity (CMS-R) framework is developed using spaceborne global navigation satellite system-reflectometry (GNSS-R) observations from the Tianmu-1 (TM) constellation. To reduce systematic differences among global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations, a probability density function (pdf) peak alignment method is applied for reflectivity calibration. Wintertime nonmelt reflectivity is utilized as the background field, and melt occurrence is identified based on daily reflectivity anomalies. Consequently, daily 25-km mapping of surface melt over the GrIS is achieved. The results demonstrate that the calibrated reflectivity exhibits a clearer separation between melt and nonmelt conditions. A significant positive correlation was found between CMS-R anomalies and melt-day counts, with Pearson and Spearman coefficients of 0.76 and 0.75, respectively. Following calibration, the detection threshold was decreased from 3.9 to 3.6 dB, thereby increasing sensitivity to weak melt. During the intense melt event on July 19, 2024, a melt extent of approximately 580 000 km2 was estimated by CMS-R, which shows close agreement with the AMSR-derived estimate of 576 200 km2. Moreover, the CMS-R melt results are consistent with observations from 23 automatic weather stations (AWSs). These findings highlight the potential of spaceborne GNSS-R as a complementary approach to monitoring ice sheet surface melt. The CMS-R framework offers an additional perspective on melt detection alongside the existing microwave observations.
item.authors: Yongchao Zhu;Lijuan Pan;Maorong Ge;Xiaohong Zhang;Fei Gao;Xiaochuan Qu;Kegen Yu;

item.title: Theoretical Bounds on Detectability of Tunnel-Induced Subsidence Using SBAS-InSAR
item.description: Tunnel-induced ground subsidence can progressively compromise overlying infrastructure, making reliable monitoring essential for urban risk management. Although small baseline subset (SBAS)-interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables wide-area, millimeter-level deformation monitoring, its ability to detect tunnel-induced settlement is fundamentally limited by interferometric phase noise, coherence, sensor resolution, and tunnel geometry. Existing studies are largely posterior, demonstrating detection after deformation has been observed, with limited capability for a priori feasibility assessment. This article develops a theoretical framework that establishes closed-form detectability limits for tunnel-induced subsidence under SBAS-InSAR. By coupling Peck’s settlement model with a Cramér–Rao bound on interferometric phase variance and the SBAS inversion geometry, analytical expressions are derived for the minimum detectable tunnel length, width, and depth, as well as the maximum detectable depth, as functions of radar wavelength, spatial resolution, coherence, and soil properties. The bounds are evaluated across five radar bands (P, L, S, C, and X) and corroborated through SBAS time-series simulations, which show close agreement with the predicted thresholds. A Sentinel-1 case study over the Dangjin tunnel construction site in South Korea provides a relative, field-based illustration of the coherence-dependent detectability mechanism. The proposed framework delineates the blind zones of SBAS-InSAR and enables a priori assessment of monitoring feasibility, providing a principled basis for sensor selection, acquisition planning, and monitoring-cost optimization.
item.authors: Lakshmi Annamalai;Imran Ahmed Syed;Bishwajit Sharma;Arshad Jamal;

item.title: 3-D Parallel Inversion of Controlled-Source Electromagnetic Data Using Dual Unstructured Meshes
item.description: 3-D numerical inversion of controlled-source electromagnetic (CSEM) data is the current trend for geophysical prospecting. In this article, we propose a 3-D parallel inversion approach for CSEM data based on dual unstructured meshes. The forward modeling is employed using an unstructured finite element method, while the inversion problem is solved using the computationally efficient limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS) method, which employs the reciprocity theorem to compute the sensitivity. This article adopts dual unstructured meshes for forward and inverse modeling separately. The inversion mesh is used for discretizing model parameters. The forward mesh is locally refined from the inversion mesh based on frequency, field source, receiver positions, and the distance between elements and these points. This dual-mesh strategy reduces singularities at source positions and improves modeling accuracy at receiver positions without increasing the number of inversion parameters, thereby enhancing the inversion efficiency and flexibility of CSEM data with multisources and multifrequencies. Subsequently, a message passing interface (MPI)-based parallel strategy is implemented to enhance computational efficiency. The convergence and reliability of the proposed algorithm are validated through single anomaly model, basin model, and complex model cases. It is further applied to field data in Karamay region in Xinjiang, China, to test its applicability. Results demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits a certain degree of noise resistance and good reliability, further validating its practicality and robustness.
item.authors: Yixin Ye;Ruodan Yang;Zhixin Liu;Shengping Gong;Chaofeng Wu;

item.title: A Curvilinear-Grid Eikonal Framework for Passive Seismic Source Location in Anisotropic Media: Theory and Numerical Validation
item.description: The accurate localization of passive seismic sources is important for geophysical applications, such as reservoir characterization and seismic-hazard assessment. Traveltime-based location methods are widely used for this purpose, but their accuracy can be significantly affected by complex surface topography and seismic anisotropy, which alter seismic traveltimes and may lead to biased source parameters when these effects are neglected or inadequately represented. To address this issue, we develop a passive-source location framework based on a topography-dependent eikonal equation (TDEE) formulated for anisotropic media on boundary-conforming curvilinear grids. The hypocenter is determined by globally minimizing a station-pair double-difference (DD) traveltime objective function, in which the origin time is eliminated, and the origin time is subsequently estimated from the absolute-traveltime residuals with the hypocenter fixed. Synthetic experiments involving complex topography and anisotropy are conducted to evaluate the accuracy, computational performance, and sensitivity of the method to observational and modeling errors. The results show that the proposed framework provides accurate hypocenter and origin-time estimates under various model configurations, whereas neglecting topographic or anisotropic effects can produce systematic biases in the estimated source parameters. The proposed method provides an effective traveltime-based approach for passive-source location in complex topographic and anisotropic media.
item.authors: Xiaole Zhou;Haiqiang Lan;Gaoshan Guo;

item.title: DGAFNet: A Dual-Branch Gradually Cross-Attention Fusion Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
item.description: Short-term precipitation forecasting is critical for transportation, agriculture, and disaster management, where accurate and timely predictions can significantly reduce risks and improve decision-making. However, traditional methods such as numerical weather prediction (NWP) and radar echo extrapolation often fail to capture fine-grained spatiotemporal dynamics, especially under high-intensity precipitation. To alleviate this issue, we propose a dual-branch gradually cross-attention fusion network (DGAFNet) based on locality-aware SwinLSTM (LASL), which fully captures the spatiotemporal evolution of precipitation by integrating multisource data from radar and satellite observations. In DGAFNet, the satellite branch is tailored to model global–local spatial dependencies, while the radar branch is specifically designed to exploit multiscale features by utilizing atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP). In addition, we introduce a gradually cross-attention fusion module (GCAFM), which leverages attention mechanisms to adaptively highlight key informative regions and dynamically merges features from the dual branches at multiple levels. Experimental results on the storm event imagery (SEVIR) dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art models (ConvLSTM, PredRNN++, SwinLSTM-B and CM-STJointNet) across metrics, especially under high-intensity precipitation scenarios. These results highlight DGAFNets ability to effectively combine multisource data for more accurate and timely precipitation forecasting.
item.authors: Haofeng Jiang;Yongfang Wang;Yanqing Zhang;

item.title: Surrogate-Assisted Physics-Guided Retrieval of Range-Varying Evaporation Duct Height From Radar Sea Clutter
item.description: Retrieving a range-varying evaporation duct height (EDH) trajectory from radar sea clutter is ill-posed, while repeatedly coupling a high-fidelity propagation solver to inversion is computationally prohibitive. This article presents Physics-ResCNN, a surrogate-assisted framework that transfers parabolic-equation (PE) knowledge to inverse-model training without adding environmental covariates or forward calculations at deployment. A residual-convolutional surrogate first learns the mapping from range-dependent duct states to PE propagation loss. Once frozen, it combines with a sea-clutter observation model to penalize disagreement between the observed clutter and that reconstructed from the retrieved duct profile. The resulting inverse network maps a 500-point centered clutter profile directly to a 101-node EDH trajectory and duct-presence mask. On a leakage-controlled, day-grouped East China Sea synthetic benchmark for 2025 under a fixed radar configuration with 3571 test profiles, Physics-ResCNN achieves 0.659-m RMSE and 0.290-m MAE, reducing RMSE by 18.6% relative to an identical supervised ResCNN. Ablation and direct-PE analyses support the observation-consistency mechanism. Buffered spatial holdouts yield smaller, seed-dependent gains than the nominal benchmark, and within-family refractivity-gradient perturbations retain lower aggregate RMSE with some tail-error reversals. The framework, therefore, provides an efficient means of embedding offline propagation physics into clutter-only, range-resolved refractivity from clutter (RFC) inference.
item.authors: Yi Yan;Jiangting Li;Lixin Guo;Yuxuan Wang;Shuji Sun;Tong Xu;Zonghua Ding;

item.title: Physics-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning Method for Nighttime AOD Retrieval With Nighttime Lights Data
item.description: Nighttime aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieval is essential for maintaining diurnal continuity in global atmospheric monitoring. However, conventional physical retrieval algorithms are often hampered by the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the single-band VIIRS day/night band (DNB) and the complex variability of anthropogenic surface illumination. These limitations frequently necessitate coarse spatial aggregation, which significantly sacrifices both spatial resolution and retrieval precision. To overcome these challenges, this study presents a novel physics-aware multimodal deep learning (DL) framework, the physics-aware CNN–Transformer (PaCT). This method adopts a standard heterogeneous decoupling architecture to process visual and scalar multimodal features: a convolutional neural network (CNN) branch extracts aerosol-induced texture degradation and background brightening from nighttime lights (NTLs) image patches, while a Transformer-based branch processes environmental scalars to characterize the radiative context. Interpretability analysis via SHAP gradients confirms that the model’s decision-making aligns closely with established physical priors. Sample-based ten-fold cross-validation demonstrates high retrieval accuracy ( $R$ = 0.938, root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 0.077), with 85.56% and 47.24% of retrievals meeting the MODIS Deep Blue (DB) expected error (EE) bounds and the global climate observing system (GCOS) stringent requirements, respectively. Notably, the PaCT framework produces retrievals at the 750-m nominal pixel spacing of the VIIRS DNB and exhibits strong consistency with various AOD products. This study effectively complements the limited spatial coverage of nighttime active lidar along-track observations, providing new data support for investigating diurnal aerosol evolution and enabling refined monitoring of urban nighttime air quality.
item.authors: Yu Sun;Lin Sun;Xiaohu Sun;

item.title: MASTrack: Motion–Appearance Semantic Tracking for Thermal Infrared Anti-UAV
item.description: Infrared anti-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) tracking faces challenges such as tiny targets, weak appearance, complex backgrounds, and rapid motion. Global tracking methods provide strong recovery capability but incur high computational costs, whereas local trackers are prone to drift under fast motion and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose MASTrack, a motion–appearance semantic tracking framework that jointly models visual appearance, historical motion, and target semantics within a local Transformer architecture. Specifically, a Mamba-based motion prompt encoder (MPE) captures long-range dynamics from historical bounding boxes, while a bidirectional motion–appearance decoder (MAD) adaptively integrates motion priors with current visual features. A SeaFormer-based segmenter further generates foreground semantics to reweight classification responses and suppress background interference. Experiments show that MASTrack achieved AUC scores of 72.11%, 64.76%, and 29.57% on the AntiUAV, AntiUAV410, and CSTAntiUAV datasets, respectively, while performing real-time tracking at 100.3 FPS, thereby validating its accuracy, robustness, and efficiency in complex infrared scenarios. Our code will be released on https://github.com/bingbing-wei/MASTrack
item.authors: Bingbing Wei;Xinying Zhang;Xu Wang;Peiwen He;Qingchuan Zhai;Yuanke Zhang;

item.title: AeroFuse: A Robust and Lightweight HSI–LiDAR Fusion Framework for Onboard Remote Sensing
item.description: Artificial intelligence and onboard computing are moving remote sensing from the traditional “acquire-then-downlink” mode toward real-time interpretation directly on airborne platforms. Since the joint data volume of hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) often exceeds the downlink budget, HSI–LiDAR fusion is increasingly expected to run onboard. Onboard fusion, however, faces three practical issues: spectral degradation caused by noise and radiometric disturbances, cross-modal spatial misalignment, and tight limits on computation, power, and latency. We present AeroFuse, a robust and lightweight fusion framework that handles each issue with a dedicated design. A geometry-anchored spectral encoder (Anchor-Enc) uses the stable LiDAR-derived geometry as a structural reference to stabilize degraded spectral features. A bidirectional bridge attention module (Bidirectional Bridge-Attn) with gated residual fusion builds feature-level cross-modal correspondence without an explicit registration module, improving tolerance to moderate spatial offsets. LiDAR Tokenization compresses the LiDAR stream into a few tokens to bound the cost of cross-modal interaction, and a lightweight conformer-based classifier operates on the resulting compact token set. Experiments on five HSI–LiDAR/DSM benchmarks (Houston, Trento, MUUFL, Houston2018, and Augsburg) show that AeroFuse achieves accuracy competitive with or better than recent fusion networks, e.g., 93.13% overall accuracy (OA) on Houston, with about 0.7 M parameters and 0.1 GFLOPs per forward pass. Additional evaluations further verify its generalization across different airborne sensing conditions. Deployment tests on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin module demonstrate the efficiency of AeroFuse for onboard HSI–LiDAR interpretation.
item.authors: Siyuan Wan;Jiuniu Wang;Mugen Peng;Yuanben Zhang;Wenjia Xu;

item.title: A Physically Consistent End-to-End Framework for Modeling and Imaging of Time-Varying Infrared Signatures of Space Targets
item.description: Infrared (IR) signature analysis of space targets is essential for space situational awareness (SSA), enabling reliable detection, identification, and characterization of objects in orbit. However, existing studies often address IR radiation modeling or imaging simulation separately, lacking a unified framework that consistently links the external thermal environment, target thermal response, IR radiation, and image formation. In this study, an end-to-end imaging framework is proposed for high-fidelity IR signature simulation of space targets. The framework integrates space external heat-flux modeling, thermal response simulation, effective IR radiation calculation, and IR image formation within a unified pipeline. Multiple radiation sources, including solar radiation, Earth thermal emission, and Earth albedo, are considered, while the influences of Earth’s underlying surface and atmospheric environment are incorporated to improve environmental realism. To validate the coupled thermal-response and IR-radiation prediction components of the proposed framework, a ground-based thermal-vacuum experiment is conducted under controlled conditions. A low-temperature environment representative of deep space is established, and combined directional heat fluxes are applied to emulate solar and Earth radiation. IR measurements in long-wave bands are acquired and compared with simulation results. The comparison demonstrates good agreement in both temporal evolution and radiative magnitude, validating the coupled radiative–thermal prediction under the prescribed boundary conditions.
item.authors: Qianwen Wang;Ruoxi Peng;Biao Zhang;

item.title: Efficient Large-Scale Remote Sensing Change Detection via Sparse Semantic Scene Graphs
item.description: Multitemporal remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is essential for large-scale postdisaster assessment, enabling rapid damage evaluation and timely emergency response. Existing RSCD approaches, especially deep-learning-based methods, often rely heavily on labeled data and dense pixel- or patch-wise comparisons, which limits cross-scene generalizability, hinders scalability to large scenes, and fails to capture the selective, object-centric, and spatially sparse nature of task-related changes. To address these issues, we propose a training-free, instance-centric, and sparse framework for large-scale RSCD based on sparse semantic scene graphs (S3Gs). The framework first reformulates large-scale RSCD as sparse instance graph reasoning by retaining only change-relevant semantic instances and local spatial relations, making direct large-area analysis computationally feasible. It then establishes instance-centric correspondence between bi-temporal S3Gs, providing greater tolerance to residual spatial misalignment. By jointly reasoning over instance semantics and relational evolution, it further infers change locations, semantic categories, and structural changes, yielding more traceable and interpretable change maps. Experiments on public benchmarks and the newly constructed large-scale natural hazards RSCD (LSNH-RSCD) dataset demonstrate both competitive accuracy and clear efficiency advantages. In particular, the proposed training-free method achieves 71.65% mean intersection over union (mIoU) on LEVIR-change detection (CD) and the best 78.33% mIoU on the hurricane subset of LSNH-RSCD, while supporting direct large-scale inference on remote sensing images (RSIs) of $7936\times 9278$ pixels in 42.54 s on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU, more than $10\times $ faster than the second-fastest baseline. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework for rapid damage assessment and large-scale disaster mapping.
item.authors: Wandong Jiang;Yuli Sun;Lin Lei;Gangyao Kuang;Kefeng Ji;

item.title: Fast Coherent Integration Detection Based on the Segment RPCA Method for Maneuvering Target in Spaceborne Bistatic Radar
item.description: Spaceborne bistatic radar has played an important role in target surveillance and reconnaissance for its advantages of broader surveillance coverage, enhanced damage resistance, and inherent spatial diversity gain. However, the bistatic configuration and target maneuverability induce significant range cell migration (RCM) and time-varying Doppler frequency modulation (DFM), which pose severe challenges to long-time coherent integration detection methods. Furthermore, existing integration detection methods, such as generalized Radon Fourier transform (GRFT), suffer from high computational complexity and storage overhead caused by the required multidimensional search operation. To address these issues, a fast coherent integration detection method based on segmented robust principal component analysis (SRPCA) is proposed, which mainly consists of intrasegment and intersegment processing. First, the keystone transform (KT) and efficient center-variant correction (CVC) are adopted to correct RCM. Subsequently, the echo is segmented along the azimuth dimension under the reasonable constraint that the Doppler spread within each segment can be neglected, and intrasegment accumulation is achieved. During intersegment processing, a rapid parameter estimation method based on the RPCA is developed to compensate for dominated higher-order phase terms. Furthermore, the higher-order phase errors are precisely compensated based on the maximum peak criterion. Therefore, well-focused results can be obtained in the range-frequency domain while reducing the computational load by avoiding multidimensional searching. Finally, to validate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method, experiments are performed by using simulated and composite data.
item.authors: Xiaoran Xie;Dong Li;Liyin Zhang;Jun Wan;Zhanye Chen;

item.title: DPEE-STGAN: A Dual-Path Encoding-Embedded Style Transfer GAN for Multidomain Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
item.description: The spectral and radiometric characteristics of remote sensing imagery can vary substantially across sensors, geographic regions, and acquisition conditions, resulting in pronounced domain shifts. Consequently, semantic segmentation models trained on a source domain often suffer severe performance degradation when directly applied to heterogeneous target-domain imagery. To address this issue, we propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive segmentation framework based on image style transfer and introduce DPEE-STGAN, a dual-path encoding-embedded style transfer generative adversarial network (GAN). DPEE-STGAN separates style conditioning into an intrinsic path that preserves source-domain geometry and texture, and an extrinsic path that injects target-domain appearance cues through hierarchical structure and color control. The resulting pseudotarget images retain the source annotations and are used to fine-tune a source-pretrained segmentation model without target-domain labels. Experiments on heterogeneous uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) and satellite datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in both style transfer and cross-domain segmentation. DPEE-STGAN achieves the lowest source-referenced learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) among the compared methods in all six evaluated transfer settings. For Potsdam $\rightarrow $ Vaihingen and Vaihingen $\rightarrow $ Potsdam, the proposed framework reaches 72.85%/48.12% and 68.43%/40.27% in overall accuracy (OA)/mIoU, respectively, improving mIoU over the corresponding source-only baselines by 12.10 and 10.41 percentage points. Across 11 additional heterogeneous target domains, the mean building intersection over union (IoU) increases from 35.20% to 50.14%. These results show that explicitly decoupling source-content preservation from target-style injection provides an effective solution for semantic segmentation under substantial remote sensing domain shifts.
item.authors: Baikai Sui;Chenxi Liu;Qingwang Wang;Zhen Zhang;

item.title: Design and Validation of an Integrated Long-Wave Infrared and Laser Detection Optical System for Space Remote Sensing
item.description: Space target detection faces key challenges, including weak-signal extraction, complex background interference, and target range acquisition. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel space target detection approach based on the synergy of infrared imaging and laser ranging. By developing an integrated dual-channel detection optical system comprising a long-wave infrared (LWIR) channel and a laser receiving channel, multisource information fusion and complementary functionality are achieved. Optical simulation results show that the LWIR channel has an F-number ( $F^{\#}$ ) of 2, and the full-field modulation transfer function (MTF) at the Nyquist frequency of 20 lp/mm exceeds 0.2 at the simulated temperatures of $0~^{\circ }$ C, $20~^{\circ }$ C, $30~^{\circ }$ C, and $40~^{\circ }$ C, approaching the diffraction limit and demonstrating good imaging performance. By optimizing the YNI and I/IBAR parameters in conjunction with LightTools stray-light analysis, the Narcissus-induced image-plane nonuniformity is effectively suppressed, resulting in a uniform focal-plane energy distribution. The laser receiving channel exhibits good energy concentration, with more than 90% encircled energy within a $40~\mu $ m diameter, and provides precise ranging capability. After integration, the dual-channel opto-mechanical system achieves a compact and miniaturized common-aperture configuration. An engineering prototype was fabricated and experimentally evaluated through wavefront testing, resolution testing, outdoor imaging, simulated space-target imaging, and laser ranging accuracy tests. The measured wavefront error after optical alignment is root-mean-square (rms) $0.067\lambda $ , and the rms static ranging error is 0.724 m (approximately 0.72 m). Ground-based imaging experiments show that the measured focal-plane grayscale distribution is consistent with the uniform energy-distribution trend predicted by the LightTools simulations, providing experimental support for the effectiveness of the Narcissus suppression design. The LWIR and laser channels provide complementary target imaging and range information, respectively, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed dual-channel integrated optical system. This work provides a practical common-aperture optical design solution for compact and highly integrated space remote sensing and space situational awareness (SSA) payloads.
item.authors: Lei Zhang;Bo Li;Jize Fan;Xu Zhang;Zihui Zhang;Xiaoxu Wang;Pingping Chen;Zhennan Li;

item.title: Physics-Informed BiLSTM Network for Atmospheric Temperature and Humidity Profiles Retrieval From Ground-Based Infrared Hyperspectral Interferometers
item.description: Atmospheric temperature and humidity profiles are essential for numerical weather prediction (NWP) and climate research. Ground-based hyperspectral infrared spectrometers provide rich radiance information, yet traditional physical retrievals are computationally expensive, while statistical approaches struggle with complex nonlinear radiance–state relationships. Purely data-driven deep learning methods improve efficiency but often lack physical consistency, limiting their reliability under unseen atmospheric conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed bidirectional long short-term memory (Phy-BiLSTM) framework to retrieve boundary-layer temperature and humidity profiles from Atmospheric Emitted Radiance Interferometer (AERI) hyperspectral radiance. The model incorporates two complementary forms of physical knowledge: 1) a BiLSTM architecture that captures vertical coupling and interlevel dependencies within the atmospheric column, physically motivated by the fact that atmospheric states are influenced by both lower and upper levels; and 2) thermodynamic consistency constraints, derived from radiative–thermodynamic balance and potential temperature continuity, which are directly embedded into the loss function during training to actively enforce physically plausible solutions. Trained on AERI and radiosonde observations from 2006 to 2016 and evaluated on an independent 2017 dataset at the Southern Great Plains (SGP) site, Phy-BiLSTM achieves root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.85 K for temperature and 1.00 g/kg for humidity, outperforming benchmark deep learning methods in capturing vertical atmospheric gradients within the 0–3 km boundary layer. Compared to the standard physical retrieval method AERIoe, Phy-BiLSTM reduces temperature and humidity RMSE by 24.1% and 23.7%, respectively, while accelerating inference from approximately 8.96 min per profile to 3.985 ms per sample on graphics processing unit (GPU)—a speedup of over 135 $000\times $ . Furthermore, long-term evaluations demonstrate the model’s robustness in reproducing the climatological annual cycle and capturing extreme events, such as the 2011 and 2012 summer heatwaves. Ablation experiments confirm that both the BiLSTM structure and thermodynamic constraints are critical to the model’s performance.
item.authors: Yangyang Song;Wanxia Deng;Lei Liu;Jinfeng Ding;Wei Huang;

item.title: Discriminating Cloud Particle Types Using Ground-Based Scanning Lidar: Theoretical Model and Experimental Analysis
item.description: Accurately identifying cloud particle types is essential for improving cloud microphysical parameterizations and remote sensing retrievals. In this study, we develop a novel discrimination method for cloud particles using scanning lidar observations near the zenith, based on the theoretical backscattering properties of ice crystals. We introduce, for the first time, the use of the coefficient of variation (CV) and the coefficient of variation difference ( $\Delta $ CV) to quantify the variability of lidar backscatter signals during scanning. By integrating these metrics with the depolarization ratio at the zenith direction ( ${\delta }_{0}$ ) and ambient temperature, cloud particles are classified into seven categories: liquid water, liquid/mixed-phase, 2-D ice crystals (quasi-horizontally oriented), 3-D ice crystals (randomly oriented), mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals, complex irregular particles (CIP), and droxtal ice crystals. Meanwhile, based on theoretical analysis, we introduced the high-depolarization coverage (HDC) metric to improve the accuracy of distinguishing mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals from liquid water or ice-liquid mixtures. After more than six months of continuous observations, the feasibility of the new algorithm was demonstrated through comprehensive observational analyses. In addition, we also observed vertical layering of different cloud particle types within some mixed-phase clouds. In these clouds, 2-D ice crystals tend to occur in the upper regions, mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals are more common in the middle layers, while 3-D or aggregated ice crystals are typically found in the lower parts of the cloud. Our proposed observational strategy and discrimination algorithm hold promise for providing new insights into cloud microphysics, which will further contribute to future climate change studies.
item.authors: Xuanhao Zhu;Dong Liu;Zhenzhu Wang;Alexander Konoshonkin;Zhiqiang Kuang;Natalia Kustova;Yingjian Wang;

item.title: Applicability Assessment of Spherical Radiative Transfer Models for Ocean Color Remote Sensing Under Large Solar Zenith Angles
item.description: Accurate ocean–atmosphere coupled radiative transfer models (RTMs) are essential for ocean color remote sensing. However, the applicability and accuracy of RTMs under large solar zenith angles (SZAs) conditions remain insufficiently quantified. This study quantifies the applicability limits of spherical RTMs under large SZAs by confronting simulations from two representative RTMs, SMART-G and SCIATRAN, with geostationary ocean color imager (GOCI) top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiance ( $L_{t}$ ) observations. Radiative transfer simulations under large SZAs are conducted across a broad range of representative atmospheric and oceanic parameters and solar-sensor geometries. In addition, the sensitivity of simulated $L_{t}$ to key atmospheric and oceanic input parameters is systematically analyzed. Results indicate that: 1) RTM simulation accuracy deteriorates nonlinearly with increasing SZA, with a stronger wavelength dependence at large SZAs; 2) the critical SZA thresholds for accuracy deterioration are identified at approximately 73° for SMART-G and between 69° and 83° for SCIATRAN; and 3) viewing zenith angle (VZA), aerosol type and optical depth, column water vapor (CWV), and wind speed (WS) dominate the accuracy of RTM simulations under large SZAs. These findings provide quantitative constraints on the applicability of RTMs under large SZAs and offer practical guidance for ocean color remote sensing applications in polar regions and during dawn and dusk observations.
item.authors: Yongquan Wang;Huizeng Liu;Yu Zhang;Menghui Wang;Qingquan Li;Guofeng Wu;

item.title: Fast and Accurate Inversion Method of Asteroid Physical Parameters With a Lycaon Pictus Hunting Algorithm
item.description: The inversion of physical parameters of asteroids is a core technology for planetary exploration engineering. There are two key limitations to traditional approaches: the objective function is nearly flat in certain parameter subspaces, making the corresponding chi-square values almost identical, while exhaustive sampling over the entire parameter space incurs prohibitive computational costs. To address these issues, we propose weakly observable subspace theory, which proves the existence of a weakly observable subspace in the parameter space where the objective function is approximately flat, making it difficult to distinguish physical parameter vectors of asteroids with high errors. Under the guidance of this theory, we propose a fast and accurate inversion method with a Lycaon pictus hunting algorithm (LPHA). This approach is inspired by two unique hunting mechanisms of Lycaon pictus, including region lock and roaming hunt. In region lock, we use singular value decomposition (SVD) of high-order derivative information and the Hessian matrix to estimate the weakly observable subspace, which is locked as the hunting region. In roaming hunt, we perform concentrated sampling in that subspace followed by Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) refinement. This framework provides mathematical characterization of the weakly observable subspace and translates biological hunting into a sampling scheme, reducing unnecessary Monte Carlo (MC) samples. Simulation results on multiple asteroids demonstrate that LPHA achieves over 60% reduction in estimation errors while requiring only 10.13% of the computation time of the conventional LM approach. LPHA provides a fast, accurate, and theoretically grounded solution for asteroid physical parameter inversion, with broad applicability to other high-dimensional nonlinear inverse problems.
item.authors: Yangyang Li;Jin Liu;Zhiwei Kang;Xiaolin Ning;Xin Ma;Jiancheng Fang;

item.title: SGHFNet: A Saliency-Guided High-Frequency Enhancement Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Transformer-based methods have achieved promising results in infrared small target detection (IRSTD) by capturing global context and long-range spatial dependencies. However, unconstrained global interactions may weaken the responses of dim, low-contrast targets. Moreover, modeling only in the spatial domain makes it difficult to distinguish true targets from target-like noise and structured background clutter. These limitations can lead to false alarms and missed detections in complex infrared scenes. To address these challenges, we propose a saliency-guided high-frequency enhancement network (SGHFNet), which inserts a saliency-guided global fusion (SGGF) block into the encoder–decoder skip connections. The SGGF block comprises two components: 1) saliency-guided cross-attention (SGCA) introduces a saliency-guided bias to regulate cross-level channel interactions and preserve weak target responses and 2) spectral-gated feed-forward network (SGFFN) combines multiscale depthwise convolution with adaptive high-pass filtering (AHPF) to enhance target boundaries and local structures. Experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K show that SGHFNet achieves competitive performance compared with 19 representative methods. Ablation studies further show that SGCA and SGFFN provide complementary gains in target recovery and false-alarm control.

item.title: SSUC-CD: A Self-Supervised and Unsupervised Collaborative Framework for Automatic Change Detection in Multitemporal Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Automatic change detection offers the significant advantage of eliminating reliance on costly and labor-intensive manual annotation data, and has become a research hotspot in the field of remote sensing information extraction. However, existing studies typically employ self-supervised learning or unsupervised learning independently and lack self-supervised learning strategies specifically designed for change detection. To address this limitation, we propose a self-supervised and unsupervised collaborative change detection (SSUC-CD) framework, which is applicable to both homogeneous and heterogeneous remote sensing images. During each training epoch, the model first performs self-supervised learning on simulated change data, followed by unsupervised learning on real multitemporal images. First, SSUC-CD utilizes the class information in remote sensing images as the source of self-supervised signals tailored for change detection. By dynamically generating simulated change data based on the real-world multitemporal images, the model gradually learns the true ability to represent and extract change information by self-supervised learning. Second, SSUC-CD leverages unsupervised change detection learning on real-world multitemporal images to further refine the model’s change detection capability. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments were conducted across six datasets. Compared with 20 state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method significantly improves the automation level and reliability of change detection without requiring manually labeled sample data. The complete source code of this method will be made publicly available at the following website upon publication: https://github.com/huifuzhuang/SSUC-CD

item.title: SFDA-Net: Spatial–Frequency Dual-Branch Autoencoder Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
item.description: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to estimate endmember spectra and fractional abundances from mixed pixels and is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis. Despite recent advances in deep learning-based blind unmixing, three challenges remain. First, many convolutional unmixing networks rely primarily on local operations, which limits their ability to capture long-range spatial–spectral dependencies and broad spatial distribution patterns. Second, the global pooling used in some attention mechanisms may weaken pixel-level coordinate information, which is important for dense abundance estimation and the preservation of spatial structures. Third, topographic effects and nonuniform illumination cause spectral magnitude variations, which may bias abundance estimation when a single linear decoder is shared across pixels. To address these issues, we propose SFDA-Net, a spatial–frequency dual-branch autoencoder (AE) for HU. First, a dual-branch feature extraction module (DFEM) combines learnable frequency-dependent Fourier filtering with local spatial convolution. The frequency branch captures long-range spatial dependencies, whereas the spatial branch preserves local neighborhood structure. Second, a coordinate attention module (CAM) uses separate horizontal and vertical encodings to recalibrate features, thereby retaining coordinate information during feature aggregation. Third, an intensity decoupling strategy (IDS) uses scale-normalized spectra for encoder-side representation learning and restores the observed spectral norm before reconstruction in the original reflectance domain. Experiments on two simulated datasets and four real or physically rendered datasets indicate that SFDA-Net provides reliable endmember extraction and abundance estimation across the evaluated datasets.

item.title: Enhanced Denoising and Terrain Sample Densification of ICESat-2 Data Using a Bayesian Signal Model
item.description: The reliability of Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite (ICESat-2) terrain height retrieval depends heavily on effective photon denoising. However, uneven background noise often complicates conventional feature-based methods, leading to the erroneous rejection of crucial signal photons. To address this, this article introduces a Bayesian signal model (BSM) as a postprocessing framework designed to recover these misidentified photons and enhance ICESat-2/ATL08 photon-denoising accuracy, thereby increasing the number of reliable terrain height samples. The BSM innovatively leverages initial ATL08 outcomes to structure a K-nearest neighbor (KNN)-derived likelihood function, generating a robust heuristic normalized score for the retrieval of missed signal photons. Subsequently, this metric is applied within a sliding-window-based detection and refinement procedure, where the definitive identification of these missed signal photons is achieved via local Otsu thresholding constrained by ICESat-2 quality parameters to minimize the inclusion of true noise. Experimental results over large-scale regions demonstrate that, within the processing windows where the BSM performs signal recovery, the approach achieves an average overall Accuracy (OA) of 0.94, compared with 0.84 for the standard ATL08. Furthermore, after the adopted quality-control screening, the method substantially increases the density of valid terrain samples while maintaining vertical accuracy comparable to that of ATL08, validating the effectiveness of the BSM for large-scale geodetic control and digital elevation modeling. The reported denoising and terrain-retrieval metrics are therefore conditional on the adopted data-selection and quality-control procedures and should not be interpreted as global performance over the full range of ICESat-2 observations and conditions.
